Read a triangle or polygon mesh file

Source: R/mesh-readers.R
read_mesh_3d.Rd

Reads Wavefront OBJ, STL and PLY files into a mesh_3d() corner table. The reader is chosen by file extension from a registry of native parsers.

Usage

read_mesh_3d(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a .obj, .stl or .ply file.

Value

A keyed corner data frame of class ggplot3d_mesh.

Details

  • OBJ (ASCII): v vertices and f faces of any size, with v/vt/vn references, negative (relative) indices and \ line continuation; o and g names become the face attribute group. Other statements are ignored.

  • STL (ASCII or binary): every facet is a triangle; vertices with exactly equal coordinates are welded. A file whose size is 84 bytes plus 50 bytes per triangle counted in its header is read as binary, whatever its first bytes say.

  • PLY (ASCII, binary little- or big-endian): header-driven elements and properties of every scalar type; vertex x, y, z and face vertex_indices (or vertex_index). Vertex red, green, blue (and alpha) become the vertex attribute vertex_colour, face colours the face attribute face_colour; other scalar vertex properties are kept as vertex attributes.

References

Wavefront OBJ: https://paulbourke.net/dataformats/obj/. PLY (Turk): https://paulbourke.net/dataformats/ply/. STL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STL_(file_format).

Examples

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".obj")
writeLines(c("v 0 0 0", "v 1 0 0", "v 1 1 0", "v 0 1 0", "f 1 2 3 4"), path)
m <- read_mesh_3d(path)
ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_mesh_3d(data = m) + coord_3d()
